advisory.title: Sensitive Directory & Route Disclosure in Robots.txt
advisory.summary: Remove internal or secret routes from robots.txt. Enforce server-side authentication and authorization guards on all backend resources rather than relying on search crawler exclusion rules.
advisory.plain_english: The web server discloses confidential or administrative paths in Disallow directives within robots.txt, providing attackers with a roadmap of unlinked backend assets (CWE-200). This finding was CONFIRMED by the Verification Service.
advisory.impact: [severity: low] Accelerates adversarial reconnaissance by revealing administrative panels, backup endpoints, and hidden folders.
advisory.remediation_patch:
```text
# Sanitized robots.txt - exclude search engine indexing without leaking sensitive paths
User-agent: *
Disallow: /search
```
advisory.threat_vector: Automated Reconnaissance / Information Disclosure via Robots.txt

evidence.excerpt: {"missing": ["Content-Security-Policy", "Strict-Transport-Security"], "url": "https://preview.owasp-juice.shop/"}
Absence of critical HTTP defensive headers confirmed against web server

advisory.title: Missing HTTP Security Defense Headers
advisory.summary: Configure the web server to emit Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
advisory.plain_english: The web server does not send critical HTTP defensive headers (Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options). This finding was CONFIRMED by the Verification Service.
advisory.impact: [severity: medium] Leaves users exposed to Clickjacking (UI redressing), MIME confusion attacks, and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

findings.summary: Overly permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policy at https://preview.owasp-juice.shop/: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is set to '*' (CWE-346, CWE-942)

evidence.excerpt: url=https://preview.owasp-juice.shop/; Access-Control-Allow-Origin=*
Permissive CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin wildcard verified in HTTP response headers

advisory.title: Overly Permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Policy
advisory.summary: Replace the wildcard '*' with an explicit whitelist of approved origins. Do not reflect the request Origin header blindly.
advisory.plain_english: The web server responds with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, allowing arbitrary external websites to read API responses and interact cross-origin via a victim's browser (CWE-346). This finding was CONFIRMED by the Verification Service.
advisory.impact: [severity: medium] Unauthorized data exfiltration, CSRF facilitation, and disclosure of authenticated payloads to third-party domains.
advisory.threat_vector: Cross-Origin Data Theft via Client Browser
